A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PuzLM research, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. However, both end with references and contain no appendices or embedded supplement. Referenced supplementary material is unavailable, including v2's additional experiments and architectural details, limiting comparison of those aspects.

before.justification: V1 reports original puzzle-reconstruction results on ImageNet and JPwLEG, missing-piece experiments, tokenizer and backbone ablations, and token-distribution analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original reconstruction experiments and reports additional PCA-dimension and model-size analyses in Figures 5 and 6.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline remains patch extraction, PCA, k-means quantization, clockwise border tokens, lexicographic ordering, separators and an autoregressive encoder-decoder trained with cross-entropy. V2's expanded formulation and newly stated argmax decoding do not establish a different implemented algorithm.

E1.justification: The demonstrated coverage remains ImageNet 3×3, JPwLEG-3, JPwLEG-5 and ImageNet with one to three missing pieces. V2 additionally references cross-dataset generalization and larger-puzzle experiments in an unavailable supplement; their actual coverage and relationship to v1 cannot be established.

E2.justification: The JPwLEG comparison changes substantially: v2 Table 4 drops Greedy, Tabu and GA, adds DiffAssemble and VLHSA, and newly includes JPDVT and FCViT results on JPwLEG-5. The backbone comparison adds GRU. CFN in v2's ImageNet table is the retained Noroozi–Favaro method, not a new comparator.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a PCA-dimension sweep and additional backbone sizes, while its backbone comparison reports only JPwLEG-3 absolute accuracy instead of both metrics across three benchmarks. V1 explicitly identifies Pegasus for JPwLEG-5; v2 gives a default-BART description without that exception, leaving the reported backbone attribution changed or ambiguous without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds PCA-dimension sensitivity and expands backbone scaling analysis. Conversely, the supplied v2 no longer shows v1's index-wise versus element-wise reconstruction experiment, JPwLEG-5 vocabulary and tokenizer ablations, or the ImageNet/JPwLEG-5 backbone analyses. This substantially revises the questions and evidence covered by the ablation section.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests for reconstruction results. The empirical-frequency and per-puzzle averaging practices in the sequence analysis remain unchanged.

E6.justification: PuzLM's JPwLEG-3 table results change from 89.5%/82.3% absolute/perfect accuracy to 91.9%/84.5%, without sufficiently explicit backbone matching to establish a same-setting gain. JPDVT's 71.3% entry moves from perfect to absolute accuracy. V2 adds baseline, PCA and model-size results while omitting substantial earlier ablation results. ImageNet and missing-piece scores remain equivalent after percentage conversion. V2's prose incorrectly gives PuzLM 87.9% perfect accuracy, contradicting Table 4's 84.5%.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the border-token count from 4(T−1) to max(1,4B−4), resolving the single-patch case. It also adds Perfect ≤ Absolute to its training-objective reasoning. The expanded function-composition notation largely formalizes the existing pipeline; no substantial theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that lightweight discrete tokenization enables standard Seq2Seq models to reconstruct square puzzles without direct raw-image access, with competitive or superior results including eroded and missing pieces. V2's symbolic terminology and explicit contribution list retain this central scientific scope.

C2.justification: New Section 3.3 develops substantive explanations involving compatibility-driven embeddings, fixed-vocabulary train–test alignment, quantization as variance reduction and reduced storage requirements. Section 3.4 adds the interpretation that valid assignments emerge without specialized decoding. These substantially expand the mechanism arguments beyond v1's shorter rationale.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies argmax inference, scoring only non-masked pieces and random ordering in the lexicographic-order ablation. It loses v1's explicit backbone variant names and context-length table, as well as the clear Pegasus attribution for JPwLEG-5. Additional architectural and implementation details are deferred to an unavailable supplement.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens positioning beyond its earlier survey of puzzle solvers, adding thematic discussions of self-supervised pretext tasks, discrete image representations and sequence models for spatial reasoning. New references include LVLM puzzle methods, VLHSA, MaskGIT and DETR, while several earlier references disappear. The relationship to multimodal and token-based research is materially expanded.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, the abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and a five-part contribution list is added. Related work becomes thematic, and the method is reorganized into five numbered subsections with substantially expanded explanations. These are extensive narrative changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 changes from two-column to single-column presentation and redraws both pipeline diagrams. It combines three sequence-analysis plots, rearranges the retained qualitative examples, adds an architecture-comparison table and replaces the backbone results table with a parameter-count plot. The ablation figures and tokenizer table are also substantially restructured.

improvement.justification: V2 improves exposition, expands modern-baseline comparisons and adds useful PCA and model-size analyses. However, it omits useful earlier ablation evidence and explicit backbone details, and introduces the JPwLEG-3 discrepancy between 84.5% in Table 4 and 87.9% in the discussion. Additional validation is referenced only in an unavailable supplement. These benefits and losses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
